race: Formula 1 Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Welcome to The Race Weekend Podcast, and Las Vegas is absolutely buzzing on qualifying night. We have pole drama, penalties, and a street that punishes mistakes.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Exactly, and that penalty is the one line I keep coming back to all week. Kimi set the pace, but the stewards say he starts sixth.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Kimi Antonelli was fastest in qualifying, but a grid penalty hands pole position to Max Verstappen. That is the headline, and it changes everything.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Max gets the big advantage, and that is not a small thing on a street circuit. He can control the opening laps and force everyone else to react.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: The front row is Red Bull, and the street is suddenly full of danger. One mistake in the dark could cost a driver the whole race.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: It also means Mercedes have to manage the night, not just chase one perfect lap. Russell was fastest in practice after the rain, so the silver car is not sleeping.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Okay, top three. I am starting with Max because pole is not just a parking space. It is a weapon, and he has the form to use it.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: I hear you, but can anyone catch him from second on a street like this? My top pick is George Russell, and I want that in the top three loud and clear.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: He has averaged second point three at Las Vegas, with two podiums in three races. Add recent wins and championship momentum, and the safest bet is easy.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: He is fastest in second, he has two Vegas podiums in three races, and he knows this street. His average is third point seven, and Mercedes are fast enough to pressure Max.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Max is the man when the lights go out, and I am not scared of the street. He has won there, he has podiums there, and he has the car to defend the lead.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: George can make the lights count, and he has the confidence to attack from the first corner. If Max makes one small error, George will be there to punish it.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: I like George, but I am not putting him above Max when the lights go out. The third seat is where I get spicy, because I am going with Kimi Antonelli.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: That is the gamble, and I kind of love it, even if it feels a little risky. One race, one podium, and an average of third is not a bad foundation for a wildcard.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: He starts sixth, but he has car pace, a Vegas podium already, and the race to recover. On a street, a confident young driver can climb faster than the grid suggests.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: I also respect the Mercedes package, because it has been quick all season. If Kimi can keep the car clean, a top three finish is not just a dream.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Kimi has the kind of season form that makes you trust him in a chaotic race. If the first ten laps get messy, he can find a line and keep moving forward.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: That is the deep cut I love, because it is not the obvious pick. But the data says Charles has the tools, and the championship fight gives it extra heat.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Deep cut time. I want Lando in fifth, but the real story is Charles Leclerc. He starts tenth, but Ferrari have pace, and Las Vegas has been kind to him.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: I also like the Red Bull young guns, because Isack Hadjar starts fourth and has the car. Liam Lawson is steady, and Arvid Lindblad can sneak into the points.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Charles has the experience, the car, and the kind of night where he can fight through traffic. Lewis Hamilton is right behind him, and this is a real championship fight.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Pierre Gasly is my final pick, and Alpine have enough speed to get a result. He starts eighth, and if the race gets bumpy, he can use the chaos to his advantage.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Ferrari have been strong this season, and the street suits their pace. If Charles can survive the opening chaos, he can be in the mix all night.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: That is a good sign, because the last thing you want is one team owning the night. If Mercedes can keep the pace, Max will have a real problem on his hands.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: So that is the board, and it is packed with stories. The street has the final say.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: And while we are at it, F1 bosses agreed a V8 engine deal from 2030. Future fuel, present fireworks, and I am here for both.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: My top ten is Max Verstappen, George Russell, Kimi Antonelli, Lando Norris, Charles Leclerc, Lewis Hamilton, Isack Hadjar, Liam Lawson, Arvid Lindblad, and Pierre Gasly.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Las Vegas, lights out, and let's race.
